mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 12-month moving average predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as reduced discount rates enhance equity valuations and stimulate economic activity without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede economic slowdowns, triggering negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as recession risks increase and corporate earnings face downward pressure.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day returns is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) and fall in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply-constrained economic expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises and INDPRO falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST change * INDPRO change) is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative as higher borrowing costs dampen corporate earnings and consumer spending, with the signal active only in this specific regime.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in tightening cycles is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) level predicts positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as strong housing demand signals sustained economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 60-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 60-day return when HOUST rises is negative.

mechanism_narrative: An annualized CPIAUCSL above 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors price in rate hikes and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 5-day returns is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and fall in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates labor market expansion without corresponding consumer spending growth, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to weakening demand and corporate revenue concerns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and RSAFS falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (PAYEMS change * RSAFS change) is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (INDPRO falling for 2 consecutive months), S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative as reduced industrial output increases inflation and lowers corporate profits, particularly in manufacturing-intensive sectors.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods during a supply shock (INDPRO falling for 2 consecutive months), or the Rank IC for INDPRO in supply shock periods is not significantly negative (Rank IC > -0.03).
